This looks like a fix for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99139, but doesn't maintain compatibility with existing data. This PR unconditionally tightens validation, which means existing persisted objects with invalid selectors will fail API validation on a no-up update.

Validation of values in ValidateLabelSelectorRequirement needs to be made conditional so that validation of existing API objects with invalid values can tolerate the invalid values on update.

1. Add a `validateLabelValues bool` param to ValidateLabelSelectorRequirement and ValidateLabelSelector
2. For all calls to ValidateLabelSelectorRequirement and ValidateLabelSelector:
   * pass `true` when validating create requests
   * pass `true` when validating update requests where the old object passed `ValidateLabelSelector(..., true)`
   * pass `false` when validating update requests where the old object did not pass `ValidateLabelSelector(..., true)`

Because there can still be persisted data with bad label selectors, we should *also* add guards to places like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/107415 where an invalid selector could disrupt a controller or scheduler.

@liggitt Thanks again for your great patience, But I have some special ideas here. Feel free to tell me if there is something I have missed.

Now, We have just one question to impl: to check the old object select validated or not in the update circumstance. For some simple Resource Definitions such as `ClusterRole`, `PDB`, and others, There is just a simple selector in their definition, so we can just make some simple helper function to check the old object is validated or not. But the thing is a little different for more complicated Resource Definitions such as NetworkPolicy/Deployment and so on. If we want to check all the LabelSelector in resource, I think there will be more duplicate code to the path-travel action.

So like what I have done in my previous function, I think we can use a simple way with two-step to complete the check based on one thing that the old object is valid if we ignore the label value check.

We check all the old objects with **DontAllowInValidLabelValue**. If the check return non-error, that means we can use **DontAllowInValidLabelValue** to check the new object. Otherwise, we should use **AllowInValidLabelValue** to check the new object

> I think we can use a simple way with two-step to complete the check based on one thing that the old object is valid if we ignore the label value check.

I think we should tightly scope the relaxed selector validation to cases where the old objects selectors were specifically invalid, not run full validation on the old object and relax selector validation if there is *any* existing validation error

issue_context.title: kube-scheduler panics on malformed label
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

A deployment was inadvertently created with a malformed label in `requiredAffinityTerms` which appears to have caused the kube-scheduler to panic and crash.

Error from kube-scheduler pods: 
```
E0107 05:56:44.099432       1 scheduling_queue.go:547] Error getting label selectors for pod: REDACTED.
E0107 05:56:44.099573       1 runtime.go:78] Observed a panic: "invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference" (runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference)
goroutine 353 [running]:
k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.logPanic(0x1b0f760, 0x2d9c290)
            /workspace/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:74 +0x95
k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime.HandleCrash(0x0, 0x0, 0x0)
            /workspace/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/dockerized/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/runtime/runtime.go:48 +0x89
panic(0x1b0f760, 0x2d9c290)
            /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:969 +0x1b9
```

Events from REDACTED pod:
```
Events:
 ```

The first error log is from here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.20.13/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L547

When `LabelSelectorAsSelector` returns error, `selector` will be nil:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.20.13/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/helpers.go#L34-L70

Returned `selector` is passed to `util.PodMatchesTermsNamespaceAndSelector` and `util.PodMatchesTermsNamespaceAndSelector` accesses `selector.Matches`. I think `invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.20.13/pkg/scheduler/util/topologies.go#L45

If my thoughts above are correct, this bug still exists on v1.20.14 (latest version of v1.20).

> this bug still exists in the newest version in the master branch. PTAL here

This `AffinityTerm` struct is created by this `newAffinityTerm` func and `newAffinityTerm` correctly handles error from `LabelSelectorAsSelector`.  The cause of this bug in v1.20 is that we pass `selector` to `PodMatchesTermsNamespaceAndSelector` without handling an error, even though `LabelSelectorAsSelector` func returns nil as `selector` when it returns an error.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L253
So, I think this bug doesn't exist on latest master branch. What do you think

In this scenario, what's the expected k8s behavior? Both the kube-scheduler and the kube-apiserver? We're considering that if the kube-apiserver is not going to deny admission that we should add an OPA gatekeeper policy.

First of all, the value name `-api-gateway-mockservice` is not valid, if a valid name is applied, this expression can apply successfully, pods would like to find nodes with the same label pods landed.
Secondly, what do you mean `if the kube-apiserver is not going to deny admission`, what's the rule you would like to deny?

Yes, we realize that the label value is malformed. I noted that in the original post. The automation used by one of our teams didn't work correctly. Of course that is being addressed, but the deployment manifest was accepted by the kube-apiserver and the kube-scheduler attempted to process it (and crashed).

So the question is: How is this detected & handled in the event this occurs again? Ideally, the apiserver would deny admission when the manifest is submitted thus letting the user know that there is an issue and correct it. If the apiserver doesn't deny, then what will the scheduler do? Just log the event (as shown above) and not panic (once 1.20 is patched)?

Clearly, the scheduler has a rule implemented to validate the label value:

`a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyValue',  or 'my_value',  or '12345', regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?').`

Ideally, the apiserver would implement the same validation rule. If the apiserver doesn't implement that rule post 1.20, then we're thinking to add an OPA Gatekeeper policy to cause such a manifest to be denied admission as it would be better to detect such issues earlier.

IIRC, `a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyValue', or 'my_value', or '12345', regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?').`  this error is emitted by the api-server. 

IMO, these errors or even panics are something we want to avoid, so syntax validations should take effect firstly before whatever admission controller(feature related) or OPA works. So if we find anything works not properly, we should patch a bug fix as this issue does.

As for whether api-server or scheduler should implement validation rules, I think the principle is `fail fast`, kubernetes is open for better implements.

Some poor thoughts.

> this error is emitted by the api-server.

It appears that error (event) was emitted by the kube-scheduler (see initial post above). If the kube-apiserver detected the error, then the manifest should have been rejected and the kube-scheduler would never have tried to schedule a pod in that deployment.

So it would seem that the apiserver needs an update to catch such malformed label values. It does that in `metadata.labels`, but not in `labelSelector` sections.

With malformed `metadata.labels: { release: -api-gateway-mockservice }`:

`The Deployment "label-test" is invalid: metadata.labels: Invalid value: "-api-gateway-mockservice": a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyValue',  or 'my_value',  or '12345', regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?')`

With the above malformed `affinity`, the apiserver accepted the Deployment.
Patching the apiserver would definitely be the preferred solution as that would cover all clusters without the need to add an OPA Gatekeeper policy.
